newsitem.title: DOMINICAN REPUBLIC: Dominican Republic suspends deportation of Haitians.
newsitem.headline: Dominican Republic suspends deportation of Haitians.

text.p: Dominican officials said on Wednesday they had temporarily suspended deportations of Haitians believed to be in the country illegally and invited international observers to supervise any future deportations.
Haitian officials and human rights workers sharply criticised Dominican authorities for alleged poor treatment of thousands of Haitians who were shipped back to their homeland in recent months.
Thousands of Haitians were repatriated this year, including many said to be Dominican citizens of Haitian descent forced to leave the country just before presidential elections earlier this year.

In the past two months, some 14,000 Haitians, many of whom claimed they were in the Dominican Republic legally, were forced to return to Haiti. Dominican officials insisted the Haitians were treated fairly, and denied any Dominican citizens were expelled.

The two nations share the Caribbean island Hispaniola, but have had strained relations for most of the past six decades. Workers from Haiti, the hemisphere's poorest nation, historically have taken unskilled jobs in the Dominican sugar industry, but faced sharp prejudice from their lighter-skinned Dominican neighbours.
